_readme: Rulings that may also apply to cards they don't name. Only groups with "status": "approved" are shown on the site (on card pages, under 'Rulings that may also apply'); "rejected" groups stay here so they aren't suggested again; groups with no status are still waiting for review. Each entry: a ruling id, the mechanic it covers, and groups of cards (strong = clearly the same mechanic, possible = worth a look). A group can also have "match": {"pilotPrimaryArcsOnly": [arcs]} to add every pilot whose primary attacks all use those arcs (at least one besides the bullseye arc), or "match": {"upgradeWithTypes": 2, "excludeTypes": [types]} for every upgrade with two or more types (leaving out the listed types), or "match": {"cardType": "Remote"} for every card of a type, or "match": {"pilotLinkedAfter": "focus"} for pilots with a linked action after that one, or "match": {"pilotAgility": 0} for every pilot with that agility, or "match": {"pilotBaseSize": "Huge"} for every pilot of that base size. See docs/related-rulings-review.md.

rr-1.mechanic: A {frontarc} attack is one that uses the {frontarc} icon on the ship card. Ships with only {singleturretarc} or {fullfrontarc} attacks can't use effects that need one; that's different from checking whether the defender is in your {frontarc}.

groups.why: Needs you to perform a {frontarc} attack
Needs you to perform a {frontarc} attack (left out in review)
Checks whether the defender is in your {frontarc} on a special weapon (added in review)
Pilots whose primary attacks are only {singleturretarc}, {doubleturretarc} or {fullfrontarc} (added in review; found from each pilot's attack arcs, so new pilots join automatically)
Checks whether the defender is in your {frontarc} (the other half of the ruling)
Checks whether the defender is in your {frontarc} (left out in review)
Gives, moves or changes a {frontarc} attack
Gives, moves or changes a {frontarc} attack (left out in review)

rr-21.mechanic: Rerolling dice is not rolling dice: effects that trigger before or after rolling dice don't trigger on a reroll.

groups.why: Same ability as the Count Dooku named in the ruling
Triggers after dice are rolled
Triggers before dice are rolled
Says it works after you roll or reroll (an exception the ruling helps explain)

rr-102.mechanic: Gaining two or more tokens from one effect is a single instance of gaining tokens, so "after you gain a token" abilities trigger once.

groups.why: Triggers after a ship gains or receives a token
Triggers after a ship gains or receives a token (left out in review: a ship can't gain more than 1 cloak token)
Triggers after a ship gains or receives a token (removed in review: Jek's ability works on each stress token he receives)
Gives a ship two or more tokens at once
Gives a ship two different tokens at once (left out in review)

rr-101.onHold: Waiting on the rules team (Nov 21, 2026): nothing here is linked until they answer.
rr-101.mechanic: "While you perform an attack" effects end when the attack ends: the Aftermath step isn't part of the attack, so a bonus attack made then isn't affected by them.

groups.why: Has an effect that lasts "during this attack"
Gives a bonus attack after an attack or after defending (in the Aftermath step)

rr-87.mechanic: An ability that refers to an upgrade type also works with upgrades that have that type plus another one (but slots granted like Weapon Hardpoint's don't work this way).

groups.why: Refers to an equipped upgrade of a type that some multi-type upgrades share ({missile}, {payload}, {modification})
Refers to an equipped {configuration} upgrade (left out in review: no multi-type configuration can go on an X-wing)
Grants a special upgrade slot, like Weapon Hardpoint
Upgrades with two or more types (found from each upgrade's types, so new ones join automatically)

rr-71.mechanic: A maximum on the number of dice rolled is applied after every effect that adds or removes dice, whatever order they were used in.

groups.why: Sets a maximum number of dice to roll

rr-65.mechanic: When a replacement effect (like Overseer Yushyn) swaps a token a ship gains as part of a cost, the effect still resolves; but "after you gain a disarm token" abilities don't trigger.

groups.why: Replaces a token a ship would gain, like Overseer Yushyn
Gains a disarm token as part of a cost, like Foreman Proach and Quinn Jast
Triggers after you gain a disarm token
Lets ships choose to gain a disarm token along with another token

rr-49.mechanic: Attacks with the ordnance icon never get range bonuses, so effects that apply a range bonus can't add one to them.

groups.why: Applies a range bonus the attack wouldn't normally get
Prevents range bonuses
Cares whether an attack has the range bonus

rr-56.mechanic: An effect that recovers charges only recovers them on its own card, unless it says otherwise.

groups.why: Recovers charges without saying which card, so only on itself (like Elusive)
Says it recovers charges on another card (the exception, like Chopper)

rr-30.mechanic: An ionized ship can only perform the {focus} action, even when an ability grants it a different action after it executes a maneuver.

groups.why: Grants a non-{focus} action after you execute a maneuver
Grants an action only after a speed 2+ or red maneuver (an ion maneuver is speed 1 and blue, so these matter only if the ship becomes ionized during its activation)
Lets other ships perform an action
Spends {force} to perform another action (added in review)

rr-59.mechanic: "Treating it as red" can be used on a red action but not a purple one, because purple is more difficult than red.

groups.why: Lets a ship perform an action of any color, treating it as red
Lets a ship perform an action of any color, treating it as red (left out in review)
Treats an action as white (the same question for a red or purple action)

rr-58.mechanic: An ability that copies another ship's action copies only the first action it performed, not a linked action after it.

groups.why: Performs the action another ship just performed
Makes coordinated ships all perform the same action

rr-92.mechanic: When an effect has an enemy ship perform an action, that ship's controller chooses the action.

groups.why: Lets an enemy ship perform an action

rr-60.mechanic: Effects that change "a barrel roll" also change the barrel roll from becoming tractored; the player who assigned the tractor token places the template.

groups.why: Changes or allows something while you barrel roll (any barrel roll, not only the action)
Changes only a {barrelroll} action, so it doesn't apply to a tractor barrel roll (the other side of the ruling)

rr-76.mechanic: Abilities that drop or launch a device without saying "if you have not dropped or launched a device this round" can give a ship a second device in the same round.

groups.why: Drops or launches a device outside the usual once-per-round limit (no "if you have not dropped..." condition)
Has the "if you have not dropped or launched a device this round" limit, like Edon Kappehl

rr-63.mechanic: A ship places only one device during the System Phase, but an ability without the "if you have not dropped or launched a device this round" condition can still drop another one later that round.

groups.why: Drops or launches a device after the System Phase, with no "if you have not dropped..." condition
Has the "if you have not dropped or launched a device this round" limit, like Edon Kappehl and "Genius"
Drops a device during the System Phase (the one device a ship can place then)

rr-104.mechanic: Thermal Detonators are dropped one at a time, so each one is its own instance of dropping a device: "after you drop a device" abilities trigger for each.

groups.why: Triggers after you drop or launch a device
Triggers after you drop or launch a device (left out in review: these ships can't drop more than 1 device in a round)
Changes the template or placement of a device you drop (used for each Thermal Detonator separately)
Drops one bomb after an attack or when destroyed, like Paige Tico (Crew)

rr-19.mechanic: When devices detonate at the same time, the first player resolves all of theirs, one at a time in any order, with each one's after-effects, then the next player does the same.

groups.why: A bomb that detonates at the end of the Activation Phase, so several can detonate at once
Triggers when a bomb or mine detonates, like Sabine Wren

rr-17.mechanic: When a mine that affects one ship is dropped onto two or more ships, the mine's owner chooses the one ship it affects.

groups.why: The Proximity Mine device itself (the ruling names the upgrade that drops it)
Another mine that affects only the one ship that overlaps it
Cluster Mines, Discord Missiles and the buzz droid swarm (added in review)

rr-18.mechanic: When a Cluster Mine set is dropped onto two or more ships, its owner chooses one ship for each Cluster Mine, then resolves them in any order.

groups.why: The Cluster Mine device itself (the ruling names the upgrade that drops it)

rr-15.mechanic: A placed obstacle that would overlap a ship goes underneath it, and the ship suffers its effects.

groups.why: Places another obstacle during play

rr-12.mechanic: A mine dropped overlapping a ship detonates right away, because a ship counts as overlapping anything placed underneath it.

groups.why: Drops a mine

rr-13.mechanic: Mines aren't bombs: an effect that refers to bombs (like Sabine Wren's) doesn't apply to mines.

groups.why: Another mine, so Sabine Wren doesn't affect it either
Refers only to bombs, so it doesn't work with mines

rr-14.mechanic: A fused mine that a ship moves through or overlaps loses one fuse marker instead of detonating; it detonates as normal the next time.

groups.why: Drops a mine
Puts fuse markers on mines

rr-16.mechanic: A ship can't be outside a remote's arcs if the remote has none, so "while you are not in its arc" abilities can't be used against it.

groups.why: Needs you to be outside the defender's arc (can't be used against a remote with no arcs)
Needs you to be outside the enemy's {bullseyearc} (a remote with no bullseye arc)
Every remote (added in review; found from the card type, so new remotes join automatically)

rr-22.mechanic: An effect that rerolls "all" dice or a set number of dice rerolls as many eligible dice as possible, and must use exactly that many if there are enough.

groups.why: Makes the other player reroll all dice or a set number of dice, like Saturation Salvo
Chooses or rerolls dice of one kind, which may be fewer than it names

rr-26.mechanic: When several effects change an action's color, it takes the most restrictive one: white, then red, then purple.

groups.why: Treats an action as red
Treats an action as white (another card that makes it red or purple wins)

rr-27.mechanic: An action whose color isn't stated is white, but one a ship performs "on its action bar" uses that action bar's color.

groups.why: Has its own **Action:** with no color, like Lando Calrissian (Crew)
A damage card's **Action:** Repair this card (no color, so white)
Performs an action "on its action bar", so it uses that action's color there
Performs an action "on its action bar" (left out in review)
Lets you perform an action that may not be on your action bar (so it's white)

rr-28.mechanic: An effect that changes the color of a kind of action (like Debris Gambit's red {evade}) also changes that action when it's linked to another one.

groups.why: Treats a red action of one kind as white, like Debris Gambit
Changes the color of one kind of action

rr-29.skipped: Skipped in review (Nov 22, 2026): general knowledge, doesn't need card links.
rr-29.mechanic: An ionized ship can only perform the {focus} action, so it can't perform an action linked to its {focus}.

groups.why: Adds a {focus} action linked to another action
Pilots whose action bar links another action after {focus} (found from each pilot's action bar, so new pilots join automatically)

rr-31.mechanic: The {force} for a purple action is a cost to attempt it, so it's spent even if the action fails.

groups.why: Lets you perform a purple action that can fail ({barrelroll}, {boost} or {coordinate})
Pilots with a purple {lock} on their action bar (a lock can fail)
Triggers after a ship performs a purple action (a failed action isn't performed)

rr-32.mechanic: A barrel roll or boost from an ability (not an action) can fail like the action, but its cost is a cost to resolve the effect, so it isn't paid if the move fails.

groups.why: Pays a cost to barrel roll or boost as an ability, not an action, like Anakin Skywalker
Boosts as an ability with no cost (left out in review: nothing to pay, so the ruling doesn't matter)

rr-33.mechanic: You can measure range before deciding whether to pay for an ability's longer range.

groups.why: Pays a cost to change an ability's range, like Sense

rr-34.mechanic: A card's action that needs a target fails if there's no valid target to choose.

groups.why: Has its own **Action:** that must choose a ship or object

rr-2.mechanic: A {frontarc} attack isn't an attack from your {singleturretarc}, even when the turret arc indicator points to your front.

groups.why: Needs a {singleturretarc} you haven't attacked from this round, like Veteran Turret Gunner
Gives a {singleturretarc} bonus attack after a {frontarc} attack

rr-3.mechanic: A ship isn't in its own firing arc, so "a friendly ship in your arc" never means yourself.

groups.why: Affects a friendly ship in one of your arcs

rr-4.mechanic: A firing arc extends to range 3 even if the weapon using it doesn't, so "in your firing arc" checks reach range 1-3.

groups.why: Checks whether a ship is in your firing arc, without a range of its own

rr-5.mechanic: A ship that can't be placed where its own effect says (like Boba Fett's) is placed within range 1 of its player's edge instead.

groups.why: Starts in reserve and is placed with restrictions, like Boba Fett (Crew)
Places a ship from reserve later in the game, with restrictions
Places a ship from reserve later in the game (left out in review: her text already places her at her player edge)

rr-6.mechanic: A special slot like Weapon Hardpoint's holds one upgrade that exactly matches one of its icons, so it can't hold an upgrade that needs more than one slot.

groups.why: Grants a special upgrade slot, like Weapon Hardpoint
A {missile} upgrade that needs a second slot, so it can't go in that special slot

rr-7.mechanic: While locking you must choose another valid object if there is one; a lock only fails when there's no valid object.

groups.why: Changes which objects you can lock, or forces a lock

rr-8.mechanic: Extra locks (like R3 Astromech's) must be on different objects, so if two of them end up on the same ship, one breaks.

groups.why: Lets you maintain more than one lock, like R3 Astromech

Transfers tokens that can include a lock

rr-9.mechanic: An effect that gives a ship an additional lock gives a lock of the same number, so the ship usually still has only one.

groups.why: The other version of Petty Officer Thanisson (Crew), with the same text

rr-10.mechanic: A lock is a token of the ship it's assigned to (so it's among that ship's "your tokens"), while "your lock" means the lock your ship assigned.

rr-83.mechanic: When "after you execute a maneuver" effects and an enemy's "after an enemy ship executes a maneuver" attack trigger together, the first player's effects resolve first; if a ship moves out of range or arc first, the attack can't be performed.

rr-43.mechanic: Requirements must be met when an ability is queued and again when it resolves; being in arc and range for a triggered attack is a requirement.

groups.why: Bonus attack after an enemy ship executes a maneuver, like Snap Shot

rr-44.skipped: Reviewed (Nov 25, 2026): general rule, applies to too many cards to link.
rr-44.mechanic: An ability's costs are paid when it resolves; if they can't all be paid, none are and the ability is removed from the queue.

rr-45.mechanic: Optional abilities enter the queue automatically when triggered, if their requirements could be met.

groups.why: Mentioned in the ruling but not linked

rr-46.mechanic: Optional abilities in the queue stay optional; the player decides whether to use each one when it's reached.

groups.why: Mentioned in the ruling but not linked

rr-47.skipped: Reviewed (Nov 25, 2026): general rule, applies to too many cards to link.
rr-47.mechanic: For "may choose a ship" abilities, the player may measure range before paying costs, then choose a valid ship or none (and pay nothing).

rr-48.mechanic: An effect that moves upgrades between ships can't give a ship an upgrade it couldn't equip.

groups.why: Moves an equipped upgrade to another ship

rr-50.mechanic: Any attack besides a ship's standard attack when it engages is a bonus attack, even if the card doesn't say "bonus".

groups.why: Grants an attack without calling it a bonus attack

rr-51.mechanic: Han Solo's attack happens at initiative 7 before any ship engages, so it always comes first, even for a ship that engages at initiative 7.

groups.why: Attacks at a set initiative, like Han Solo (forum-106 rules that Corran's order is free)

forum-106.mechanic: A ship with an "at initiative 0" bonus attack that engages at initiative 0 may perform its two attacks in either order.

groups.why: Attacks at a set initiative (rr-51 rules that Han Solo's attack always comes first)
Changes the initiative a ship engages at, like Torkil Mux

forum-104.mechanic: Abilities that trigger after the same action enter the queue together, and their controller chooses the order.

forum-103.mechanic: A ship that ignores an obstacle while it moves doesn't skip its Perform Action step for overlapping it.

forum-101.mechanic: A lock transferred to a ship that can't be locked is removed from the first ship, then breaks.

forum-100.mechanic: A lock transferred to another ship counts as the enemy ship locking that ship, so "after an enemy ship locks you" effects trigger.

forum-96.mechanic: "Before you execute a maneuver" abilities that change the maneuver enter the queue together; the player picks the order, so Interloper Turn can resolve before Precision Ion Engines changes the maneuver.

forum-99.mechanic: Restricted cards aren't limited, so a restricted {illicit} upgrade can go under the Razor Crest title.

Drops or launches an obstacle that can be placed under a ship

forum-94.mechanic: An ability with a cost can only enter the queue if its cost can be paid when it triggers.

rr-69.mechanic: Sets a ship's dial to a new maneuver after it is revealed (the new maneuver becomes the revealed maneuver).

groups.why: Sets a dial to a different maneuver after it's revealed
Checks the speed, bearing or color of your (or another ship's) revealed maneuver
Triggers on revealing a maneuver of a certain color (Hera Syndulla is listed above)

rr-84.mechanic: When changes to a revealed maneuver's speed, difficulty or bearing apply (Reveal Dial vs Execute Maneuver), and that changing a maneuver without setting the dial doesn't change the revealed maneuver.

groups.why: Sets a dial to a different maneuver after it's revealed
Increases or decreases a maneuver's difficulty
Executes a different maneuver than the one revealed, without setting the dial
Treats purple maneuvers as red

rr-68.mechanic: A revealed maneuver's difficulty, speed and bearing are its printed ones: effects that change the difficulty don't change what's checked.

groups.why: Checks the speed, bearing or color of your (or another ship's) revealed maneuver
Triggers on revealing a maneuver of a certain color
Changes maneuver difficulty (the other side of this ruling)

rr-37.mechanic: Flipping a dial faceup is not revealing it.

groups.why: Flips a dial faceup
Looks at a ship's dial (added in review: the same ruling applies)

rr-25.mechanic: Purple maneuvers can't have their difficulty changed, but can be treated as another color.

groups.why: Treats purple maneuvers as red
